items.title: Warning if package was orphaned then adopted
items.body: This is an idea to help protect against [AUR compromises](https://lists.archlinux.org/archives/list/aur-general@lists.archlinux.org/thread/FGXPCB3ZVCJIV7FX323SBAX2JHYB7ZS4/#5FDTMKA54RMWNRHJFUAKXEBAFV5WPDUL). I propose paru displays a loud warning when trying to install or upgrade a package that was orphaned and then adopted. Showing it in color in the initial confirmation screen, before jumping to the PKGBUILD diff review, would make it easier to spot.

items.title: Make it possible to keep build dependencies during orphan removal.
items.body:
Deleting build dependencies(`makedepends`) during system update is annoying.

I want to keep them during orphan removal.

Can paru do that?

items.title: paru (sometimes?) rebuilds package from scratch after sudo timeout
items.body:
### Affected Version
**paru -V**

paru v2.1.0 - libalpm v16.0.1

### Description
**Have you checked previous issues?**

This is a continuation of #1401, which I cannot reopen due to permissions on the repository. To recap: after building a package, paru uses sudo to install it. sudo by default times out waiting for a password after 5 minutes. paru exits unsuccessfully when this happens. Rerunning paru causes it (possibly not in all cases) to start over building the package.

Side note: obviously it is more likely that sudo will time out if it's left unattended, which is more likely when the package takes a long time to build. So this issue is most likely to affect package builds that are already time-consuming.

Response from @Morganamilo on the previous issue:

> Paru caches so the sensible thing to do is just re run your command.

[...]

> It's always been like that. There's just some startup time where paru first checks if there's a new version of the package and stuff. But it won't rebuild the whole packages.

After learning this, I played around with paru a little bit, and found that this statement *seemed* to be correct. So for a while, I began thinking that I had simply gone crazy and full imagined all and any of this having ever happened. However, I just ran into it again just now, so I think that the caching must be broken in certain situations.

### Output
**Include the FULL output of any relevant commands/configs**

**Don't cut parts of the input always include the FULL thing**

**paru.conf and pacman.conf are usually always relevant**

Here is the terminal output from the following sequence of events:

1. I ask paru to install `grafana-bin`.
2. I leave to do other things.
3. The package is built successfully.
4. sudo prompts me for my password. As I am not present, it times out, causing paru to fail.
5. I return, notice the error, and ask paru to install `grafana-bin`, again.
7. I notice that paru does not install the ready-built package, and is running makepkg again.
8. I kill paru, and verify that the package is already built, and is in paru's cache.

Is it perhaps because I was installing this package for the first time on this system (and not upgrading it)? Did I pick the wrong moon phase to do this under? bridge-utils 1.7.1-2

```
lib32-gtk3 1:3.24.48-1
libxcrypt-compat 4.4.38-1
```

**paru -c**
```
checking dependencies...

Packages (1) bridge-utils-1.7.1-2

Total Removed Size:  0.03 MiB

:: Do you want to remove these packages? [Y/n]
```

I investigated the `libxcrypt-compat` package:

**paru -Qi libxcrypt-compat**
```
Name            : libxcrypt-compat
Version         : 4.4.38-1
Description     : Modern library for one-way hashing of passwords - legacy API functions
Architecture    : x86_64
URL             : https://github.com/besser82/libxcrypt/
Licenses        : LGPL
Groups          : None
Provides        : libcrypt.so=1-64
Depends On      : libxcrypt
Optional Deps   : None
Required By     : None
Optional For    : None
Conflicts With  : None
Replaces        : None
Installed Size  : 174.02 KiB
Packager        : Christian Hesse <eworm@archlinux.org>
Build Date      : Tue 14 Jan 2025 04:23:12 PM CET
Install Date    : Thu 16 Jan 2025 10:30:17 PM CET
Install Reason  : Installed as a dependency for another package
Install Script  : Yes
Validated By    : Signature
```

It's not required or optional for anything, but provides `libcrypt.so=1-64`. Using `pyalpm` I extracted installed packages that depend on `libcrypt.so` in any version:
```
alpm.Package("openssh-9.9p1-2-x86_64") libcrypt.so=2-64
alpm.Package("pam-1.7.0-2-x86_64") libcrypt.so=2-64
alpm.Package("perl-5.40.1-1-x86_64") libcrypt.so=2-64
alpm.Package("shadow-4.16.0-1-x86_64") libcrypt.so=2-64
alpm.Package("systemd-257.3-1-x86_64") libcrypt.so=2-64
alpm.Package("util-linux-2.40.4-1-x86_64") libcrypt.so=2-64
```

All of them depend on version `2-64` which isn't what the package provides. This suggests that version isn't taken into account for cleanup logic. After digging through the code I found this: https://github.com/Morganamilo/paru/blob/55efaabda3567908c3875cea0dcd3f47847896b3/src/util.rs#L174

The code ignores provider version which seems to be taken into account when finding "real orphans".

Just to be sure I checked if anything provides the correct version on my system:
```
alpm.Package("libxcrypt-4.4.38-1-x86_64") libcrypt.so=2-64
alpm.Package("libxcrypt-compat-4.4.38-1-x86_64") libcrypt.so=1-64
```

Yep, another package provides that version. My conclusion - when looking for packages to remove during `paru -c`, provider versions need to be checked against dependency version requirements.

items.title: reversed sort order compared to yay
items.body:
I am used to the sort order of search results in yay: 

```
15# yay amdgpu
41 aur/amdgpu-clocks-git r28.02492e9-1 (+0 0.00) 
    Simple script to control power states of amdgpu driven GPUs
40 aur/python-pyamdgpuinfo 2.1.0-1 (+0 0.00) (Orphaned) 
    AMD GPU stats
...
2 aur/opencl-amdgpu-pro-pal 20.30_1109583-1 (+93 1.50) (Orphaned) (Out-of-date: 2020-10-02) 
    AMDGPU Pro OpenCL driver PAL
1 extra/xf86-video-amdgpu 19.1.0-2 (71.3 KiB 165.7 KiB) [xorg-drivers] (Installed)
    X.org amdgpu video driver
==> Packages to install (eg: 1 2 3, 1-3 or ^4)
```

This is convenient because the lower numbers with the best matches are at the bottom and I can immediately see them.

With `paru` the sort order is reversed. And I have the highest numbers at the bottom and the lowest numbers at the top. This is inconvenient if the list is long because then I have to scroll up to see the best matches:

```
16# paru amdgpu
 1 extra/xf86-video-amdgpu 19.1.0-2 [71.29KB 165.72KB] [Installed] (xorg-drivers)
    X.org amdgpu video driver
 2 aur/amdgpu-core-meta 20.30_1109583-1 [+93 ~1.50] [Orphaned]
    Config file /etc/ld.so.conf.d/20-amdgpu.conf
...
40 aur/lact-git r17.5eac31b-1 [+0 ~0.00]
    AMDGPU Controller application
41 aur/aomp-amdgpu 11.11.0-1 [+0 ~0.00]
    Clang/LLVM based compiler with added support for the OpenMP API on Radeon GPUs
:: Packages to install (eg: 1 2 3, 1-3 or ^4): 
```

Is this behavior intentional? If yes, can you please make it configurable?

items.title: Connection reset by peer while downloading large number of PKGBUILDs
items.body:
I've found when attempting to update my system after many packages have built up, the download fails after maybe 40-60 PKGBUILDs in sequence. 
The only other issue mentioning such an error is #770 and specifically points to gitconfig, I've included grep output below showing i have no such lines in mine. 
I'm sure if i tried enough times it may finish, but I also can get through just by going 30 packages or so at a time, its quite a hassle though.
Considering how many aur packages I have pending update and the fact it times out part way through the download I'm assuming this is some form of rate limiting given the web attacks on the aur, as that's around when it started for me.

items.body:
### Affected Version
paru v2.1.0 - libalpm v15.0.0


### Description

items.title: Move packages status step to the previous one
items.body:
**Have you checked the readme and man page for this feature?** Yes
**Have you checked previous issues for this feature?** Yes

Currently there's a step showing this:
```
:: packages not in the AUR: […]
:: marked out of date: […]
:: orphans: […]
```
But this step appears right after the list of packages to upgrade and the choice of what should be skipped.
Considering this can have some influence on what we pick here, I think it would be more appropriate to move this before the list, and before user make choices of what to upgrade/skip.

This could also see some little improvement on readability: currently the lists have standard colors while the "categories" (what I quoted) is in bold white, leading to have this obvious while the packages names aren't se obvious from a quick read through.

EDIT: This is not exactly original's message topic, but this:
```
Total Download Size:
Total Installed Size:
Net Upgrade Size:
```
could also come before confirmation.

items.title: Search packages by the `Provides` field
items.body:
**Have you checked the readme and man page for this feature?**  yes
**Have you checked previous issues for this feature?**  yes

There is a similar issue: #873

I want to search python interpreters on AUR, however it fails because there are too many packages have "python" in their names:

``` shell
$ paru -Ss --searchby name python
error: aur search failed: Too many package results.
```

On the other hand, AUR web displays packages those provide python if python is a dependency. For example: https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/ipython-git

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53637421/226461512-719f109d-13ce-481c-b3c3-8f2b2fb51e76.png)

It would be great to have a `--searchby provides` feature:

``` shell
$ paru -Ss --searchby provides python
aur/python32 3.2.6-4 [+0 ~0.00]
    Next generation of the python high-level scripting language
aur/nogil-python 3.9.10+1+5c35dc0-1 [+0 ~0.00] [Orphaned]
    Python Multithreading without GIL
aur/python36 3.6.15-5 [+35 ~0.00]
    Major release 3.6 of the Python high-level programming language
aur/python38 3.8.16-3 [+26 ~0.21]
    Major release 3.8 of the Python high-level programming language
aur/python312 3.12.0a5-1 [+1 ~0.28]
    Major release 3.12 of the Python high-level programming language
aur/python311 3.11.2-1 [+6 ~0.66]
    Major release 3.11 of the Python high-level programming language
aur/python39 3.9.16-2 [+18 ~0.79]
    Major release 3.9 of the Python high-level programming language
aur/python37 3.7.16-1 [+31 ~0.82]
    Major release 3.7 of the Python high-level programming language
core/python 3.10.10-1 [0B 55.25MiB] [Installed]
    Next generation of the python high-level scripting language
```

The infomation is available in https://aur.archlinux.org/packages-meta-ext-v1.json.gz. For example, it's `python311`:

``` json
{
    "ID": 1219566,
    "Name": "python311",
    "PackageBaseID": 171761,
    "PackageBase": "python311",
    "Version": "3.11.2-1",
    "Description": "Major release 3.11 of the Python high-level programming language",
    "URL": "https://www.python.org/",
    "NumVotes": 6,
    "Popularity": 0.66288,
    "OutOfDate": null,
    "Maintainer": "rixx",
    "Submitter": "rixx",
    "FirstSubmitted": 1633623017,
    "LastModified": 1677683845,
    "URLPath": "/cgit/aur.git/snapshot/python311.tar.gz",
    "Depends": ["bzip2", "expat", "gdbm", "libffi", "libnsl", "libxcrypt", "openssl", "zlib"],
    "MakeDepends": ["bluez-libs", "mpdecimal", "gdb"],
    "OptDepends": ["sqlite", "mpdecimal", "xz", "tk"],
    "Provides": ["python=3.11.2"],
    "License": ["custom"]

```

items.title: BatchInstall does not work
items.body:
### Affected Version
1.8.2

### Description
Its hard to tell exactly the order of things because there is so much output, but after putting BatchInstall in my /etc/paru.conf and my ~/.config/paru/paru.conf I can confirm that it is downloading, compiling, and installing each package one at a time. When using yay I found that the batch install option was very important after installing some packages with many dependencies, if one of the compilations failed then you would not have a bunch of stray packages that aren't considered orphans. items.title: Option to mark makedeps as dependencies for AUR packages
items.body:
**Have you checked the readme and man page for this feature?**
Yes
**Have you checked previous issues for this feature?**
Yes

Would it be possible to add an option in `paru.conf` to mark makedeps as dependencies of AUR packages? This would be helpful for pruning orphaned packages without needing to reinstall makedeps every time an AUR package is upgraded, and also removing unneeded ones when no installed AUR packages use it.
